body.v: Your ThisIsTea password expires today at 17:00. Sign in now to keep your current password.

hotspots.explain: Read the address from the right: the owner is the end of the domain, here secure-login.example. The thisistea.example at the front is just set dressing.
"Expires today": an invented deadline to rush you.
A 17:00 cut-off leaves you barely any time to check. A real password change does not come with a same-day threat.
The link plays the same trick: thisistea.example.secure-login.example belongs to secure-login.example.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone borrowing ThisIsTea's name. The real owner of the address is secure-login.example; the thisistea.example to its left is just set dressing.

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Fear and haste: unless you act right now, you lose your password today at 17:00.

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Sign in through the link to "keep" your password, which amounts to handing it to the sender.

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Skip the link. Open ThisIsTea yourself, from a bookmark or by typing the address, or ask the IT team through a channel you know.
choices: Click to see what the page looks like
Open ThisIsTea by typing the address yourself

actions.label: Open ThisIsTea by typing the address yourself, and ask the IT team if in doubt
actions.consequence: Your password is not expiring at all. The email was fake.

actions.label: Click the link and sign in
actions.consequence: The page copies your login details for the scammer.

actions.label: Reply to the helpdesk address
actions.consequence: Your reply lands with the scammer, who is delighted to chat.

actions.label: Report it to the IT team so they can warn your colleagues
actions.consequence: The IT team can alert everyone before someone else clicks.

attacker_reveal: I put thisistea.example at the start of the address, where the eye lands, and my real domain at the very end. Add a 17:00 deadline and few people take the time to read from the right.
